title: protocol/1

Identifier.description: A well-formed identifier is not empty, and without whitespace, control characters or Unicode format characters (general category Cf). The pattern checks only for whitespace; Canon also refuses control and Unicode format characters.

Age.description: A length of time: a whole number without leading zeros, followed by `s`, `m`, `h` or `d` (`5m`, `24h`). Canon also refuses an age too long to count in seconds.

ScalarIdentifier.description: An identifier, or a boolean or a number written unquoted, which Canon reads as its text (`true`, `2`).

format.description: The document format; the validator accepts only `protocol/1`.

invalidation.description: The invalidation rules, keyed by rule id; a protocol without the section declares none.

case.description: What a case governed by the protocol gives when it opens: its case inputs. A protocol without the section declares no input.

ProtocolHeader.description: The protocol's identity: id and revision.

Artifact.description: A thing whose revisions evidence is bound to.

EvidenceKind.description: A kind of evidence the protocol admits.

max_age.description: How old a record of this kind may be and still apply: at an evaluation instant later than its `observed_at` by more than this, it is excluded as expired (design § 8).

Claim.description: A proposition whose value is established from evidence by its predicate.

Obligation.description: Something that must be done before the case can be complete. It is discharged only when its discharge predicate, over claim values, evaluates true (design § 8). One with an applicability predicate applies only when that predicate is not false: false, it is not applicable.

applicable_when.description: When the obligation applies, over claim values and case inputs; always, when absent.

Action.description: A semantically named possibility: what it needs, what authority it requires, what effect it has and what evidence it may produce (design § 10).

Outcome.description: A legitimate terminal interpretation of a case and what it requires: a predicate, or an explicit decision (`requires: decision: <name>`).

InvalidationRule.description: An invalidation rule: a change of its upstream artifact's revision invalidates, for the claims it names and every claim built on them, the evidence observed against an earlier revision of that artifact (design § 4.1, CANON-INVALIDATION-001).

upstream.description: The artifact whose revision the rule watches.

invalidates.description: The claims whose support a change of that revision invalidates.

inputs.description: The case inputs, keyed by input id.

Predicate.description: A predicate over evidence and claim values.

all.description: True when every member is true; true when empty.

any.description: True when some member is true; false when empty.

input.description: True when the case's value of the input is one of the values listed, false otherwise.

in.description: The values the test is true for, written `in`.

first.description: Whether the first record of a kind, in the evidence history, has a result.

before.description: Whether the first record of one kind, in the evidence history, was observed strictly before the first record of another.

CapabilityRequirement.description: One capability an action requires authority for.

EvidenceProduction.description: One evidence kind an action may produce.

decision.description: The outcome is legitimate only with an explicit decision of this name, for the outcome, taken at the case snapshot's current revision.

oneOf.description: The outcome is legitimate when the predicate is `true`.

CaseInput.description: A case input: configuration a case fixes when it opens, one of a closed, non-empty list of values. Not evidence, so no evaluation has an unknown input.

values.description: The values the input may take.

EvidenceMatch.description: Matches evidence of one kind, optionally with one result, and optionally only evidence about one declared artifact: a match that names a subject reads only the records whose subject it is.

FirstResult.description: An order form: whether the first record of `kind`, about `subject` when it names one, has `result`. It reads every record of the kind the evidence check accepted, excluded or not.

kind.description: The evidence kind whose first record is read.

result.description: The result that first record is to have.

subject.description: The declared artifact the records read are about; without it, records about any artifact.

EvidenceOrder.description: An order form: whether the first record of kind `first` was observed strictly before the first record of kind `then`, both about `subject` when it names one. It reads every record of the two kinds the evidence check accepted, excluded or not.

first.description: The evidence kind whose first record is to come first.

then.description: The evidence kind whose first record is to come after it; another kind than `first`.

subject.description: The declared artifact the records of both kinds are about; without it, records about any artifact.

Truth.description: A three-valued truth value. `Unknown` is not `False`.
